commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[rl] Align Arrow text widths before combining SkyRL task inputs (#12404)

read_prompt_files passed per-source datasets straight to
datasets.concatenate_datasets, which fails with "The features can't be
aligned" when the same column is string in one source and large_string
in
another. The Mochi campaign run v2-mix-009 died at startup this way on
task_sha256, task_spec and runtime.

Widen compatible text columns to large_string before concatenation,
including all-narrow-string mixes so text columns carry one canonical
width, and keep rejecting incompatible non-text schemas. Mixed-width
Parquet regression tests verify that task JSON, hashes, routes and
numeric
values survive concatenation. Widening covers top-level columns only;
nested text, such as the source-format prompt message lists, keeps its
original width and still raises on mixed widths.

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[iris] Add researcher interactive budget tier entry (#12367)

Add a user entry to the Iris researcher budget tier (`budget_limit:
75000`, `PRIORITY_BAND_INTERACTIVE`) in `lib/iris/config/marin.yaml`.

Without an explicit entry, submissions fall back to the default 1000
interactive budget and are demoted to `PRIORITY_BAND_BATCH` whenever
active cluster spend exceeds 1000.

commits.author: chrismc91
commits.message:
[eval] Score lost sandbox command output as a failed submission (#12269)

A Daytona command whose output could not be read raised
`CommandOutputLost`, which the evaluation driver
(`marin.rollouts.evaluation.run_evaluation`) did not classify, so a
single attempt stopped a whole agentic evaluation. A 20-item SWE-bench
Verified smoke run of Muse Glimmer 30B from TaskCompendium corpora
stopped after its first attempt this way. Daytona reported `fork/exec
/usr/bin/bash: no such file or directory` for the agent's next command,
after the episode had run for many steps in a working sandbox, so the
agent had most likely damaged its own machine.

Once the harness has started, the driver now scores such an attempt as a
failed submission with reward 0, as it already does when the agent fills
the machine's disk and as Harbor scores trials whose agent broke its
environment. Before the harness starts, the error stays an unexpected
failure. A lost output caused by the provider during an episode would
also score 0; the run records the error in the attempt's evidence.

commits.author: chrismc91
commits.message:
[eval] Start likelihood contexts with the model's BOS token (#12222)

A nonempty likelihood context now starts with the tokenizer's BOS token
when the model expects one. It did not before: `encode_pair` encoded
every nonempty context with `add_special_tokens=False`. Models trained
with a leading BOS therefore scored WinoGrande, TruthfulQA MC2, BoolQ,
PIQA, LAMBADA and the other likelihood tasks on prompts they never see
in training. Rescoring gemma-4-26B-A4B-it's saved October campaign
requests with BOS raised WinoGrande accuracy by 4.97 points [1.26, 8.68]
and TruthfulQA MC2 by 6.26 [3.24, 9.36] (#12156).

The worker resolves the policy once from the tokenizer. It prepends BOS
when the tokenizer adds BOS on encode or the chat template writes
`bos_token`. The second signal is needed for Gemma 4, whose tokenizer
never adds BOS on encode although its template does. Marin's Llama 3
tokenizer (Snowball and Grug checkpoints), Glimmer and Gemma 4 gain BOS.
Qwen3.6 has no BOS token, and Nemotron 3.5 Super's template does not use
its `<s>`, so their requests are unchanged. An empty context keeps the
existing single prefix token.

Likelihood protocol versions gain `bos-2026.11.24`, so results scored
without BOS are not reused. Chat and agent protocols keep their
identities. Panel-model scores need GPU reruns of the likelihood
benchmarks and are not included here.

Part of #10828.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[shellbox] Report Daytona headroom from sandbox inventory (#11840)

API keys cannot read Daytona's organization-usage endpoint. Read every
sandbox inventory page and compare allocations with the account-owner
limits recorded in `ACCOUNT_LIMITS`
(`lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/usage_cli.py`), the single
quota source of record.

Daytona enforces quota per region, so usage is grouped by each sandbox's
`target` and headroom is sized per region against that region's recorded
limits; it is never summed across regions, and a region without recorded
limits fails the reading. The owner-supplied figures (2026-11-19) are
recorded for the `us` region, the one region Marin launches in. Compute
and disk follow the provider's separate charged-state rules, including
stopped and paused disk, transition-state compute, and compute during
resize or snapshot operations whose desired state is started.
Unclassified lifecycle metadata fails the reading. The report converts
decimal GB quotas to GiB and reserves 20% of each region's quota by
default, reporting zero additional sandboxes when a requested profile
exceeds a per-sandbox maximum.

Inventory is the standard CLI path. Standard key variables select their
quota presets: `DAYTONA_EVAL_API_KEY` for eval, `DAYTONA_RL_API_KEY` for
rl, and `DAYTONA_DATA_API_KEY` for data; custom key variables require
`--limits`. Empty inventories report zero use and a null organization
ID. The command is an optional diagnostic; the create-time quota retry
in #12389 is the enforcement path, and submitters must still retain
their admission locks and pending-create reservations.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[tasks] Apply one retry policy to every SkyRL task kind (#11850)

Transient startup failures can recover by running the task on a fresh
machine. Apply `rigging.task_errors.retry_delay` to every SkyRL task
kind through the task worker: a retry budget, name exclusions, and
jittered exponential backoff configured at
`environment.task_sessions.retry`. Only transient dispositions retry;
permanent and unknown dispositions stay terminal. Mixed-task Snowball
and Mochi recipes select one retry for every task kind, the checked-in
ultra launch allows three, and checkpoint-evaluation recipes default to
one while preserving explicit overrides.

The retry covers only attempts with no recorded rollout steps and
confirmed cleanup, so failures after sampled work keep their stored
outcome, and passthrough treatment keeps available verifier output
without another attempt.

An authored setup command now classifies itself at raise time. A
timed-out or signal-killed command is transient and retries on a fresh
machine, restoring the retry that #12167 gave setup exits in the signal
range; a normal non-zero exit is the task's own permanent failure.
`exception_identity` keeps a producer-owned disposition on the exception
unless provider status or a permanent cause decides.

Disposition decisions stay split by boundary because each owns inputs
the others lack: `daytona_error_identity` applies the Daytona backend's
rules at its own raise site, and the task worker remaps timeouts by the
rollout phase, which no exception object carries — `TaskMachineError`
stays backend-agnostic, knowing only the machine operation.

The producer error identity from #11849 (closed, folded here) lands with
it: `ErrorIdentity` carries the exception name, category, cause,
operation, provider status, and safe diagnostics for task results, and
training, archive, and scoring consumers read the stored category
without loading the producer framework.

Native Harbor keeps main's retry loop, teardown rule, and archive
behavior until the driver is deleted, so `RetrySettings` carries no
category filters and rigging pins no Harbor dispositions. Moving the
native evaluator onto the shared policy is a follow-up.

Closes #11849.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[eval] Evaluate Hero at multiple context lengths (#10711)

Hero evals score 4K and the current training length, adding fixed 65K
and 262K evals only once training reaches those lengths. Each distinct
length has its own metrics, such as
`eval_dropless/seq_len_4096/paloma/macro_loss`;
`eval_dropless/paloma/macro_loss` continues to report the
training-length eval.

All eval lengths keep the training context-parallel width. The dropless
mesh and PartitionSpec renaming reuse #10709's implementation: each
device retains its training context group and uses its training (data,
expert) group for eval data. Eval therefore reuses the device groups
whose replacement caused NCCL memory growth in #10709. Batch sizes stay
within the configured global padded-token budget per evaluation batch,
rounded down to whole batch shards.

Continuous-text validation retains incomplete final sequences with right
padding and excludes padding from attention and loss, including the
real-to-pad prediction. Short Paloma corpora remain in the long-context
aggregate. Validation sequence statistics include the final partial
sequence; stored token counts exclude padding. Overall loss and
bits-per-byte macros exclude tags with no scored tokens.

CPU tests check device groups, per-device parameter shards and the
multi-length eval-to-training handoff. No GPU rehearsal of this revision
has run.

Part of #8435.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[levanter] Bound FP32 TPU paged attention tile sizes (#12028)

Cap the query and KV tile sizes passed to JAX's Pallas paged attention
kernel for Grug's FP32 cache. The upstream long-context tiles can exceed
scoped vector memory. The caps are 128 query rows and eight KV pages.

A v5p-8 test attended to a 64K cache with 129 zero query rows and
matched
the analytical causal mean of the visible values.
[Iris
run](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fdlwh%2Fsnowball-upstream-rpa-fp32-64k-v5p-20261123)

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[levanter] Normalize policy logits on fixed FP32 row tiles (#12027)

Add a shared FP32 log-normalizer and log-softmax for vocabulary logits.
A
fixed row tile gives each token the same reduction schedule when scored
alone or in a learner batch. This prevents a change in batch shape alone
from changing policy log probabilities on TPU.

The primitive preserves leading-axis sharding and gathers vocabulary
shards
before reduction. The fused cross-entropy reference shares the accurate
reduction. Serving and learner callers can adopt the fixed tiling
separately.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[rl] Avoid redundant gcloud project setup in nightly (#12384)

Install the Cloud SDK in both SkyRL nightly jobs without running `gcloud
config set project`. The preceding WIF auth action already exports
`CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT`. The optional `project_id` input to
`setup-gcloud` triggers an extra gcloud command; in [run
45878870665](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/45878870665/job/140112802997),
its token refresh lost the connection and stopped Grug before Iris
submission.

OPD and CatCount passed in that run. The controls job separately reached
its six-hour timeout; #12370 handles controls reconciliation. The
revised setup has not yet run in a scheduled workflow.

Fixes #12383

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
Alert on failed Iris controller checkpoints (#12351)

Page when the latest periodic checkpoint upload from a CoreWeave Iris
controller fails. The controller reports each attempt as a numeric
Finelog metric, so the alert clears after a successful upload. The
runbook points to checkpoint storage credentials and explains why a
refreshed Secret can leave bundle uploads failing until the controller
replaces its startup S3 client.

RNO2A rejected its mounted access key with `InvalidAccessKeyId` on three
checkpoint attempts before recovery
([incident](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/1085)). Existing alerts
cover controller liveness and storage capacity, but a running controller
with failed checkpoint uploads had no direct alert. Node storage probes
use a different bucket. The new rule requires checkpoint telemetry to
reach the Marin hub; absent samples yield no checkpoint verdict.
